we design a mechanism that is provably secure and efficient against malicious contractors, even if a significant fraction of the contractors are malicious.

we provide a system which incentivizes rational contractors to perform outsourced computation correctly, and which guarantees high correctness even in the existence a large fraction of irrational contractors.

designing a system for incentivizing outsourced computation that is robust to a significant fraction of malicious contractors.
incentivizing rational contractors to compute outsourced jobs correctly, while tolerating the existence of malicious contractors.
incentivized outsourced computation resistant to malicious contractors.

we show how to incentivize rational contractors and deter malicious contractors, and how to do so with a small efficiency loss.
we present an efficient and provably secure outsourcing computation system that can withstand a relatively large fraction of malicious contractors.

we achieve high correctness guarantees with high efficiency even when there are a large number of irrational contractors.
we provide a practical and efficient solution to the problem of incentivizing outsourced computation.
